incidente.resumo: At a water treatment plant, the fluoride feed pump was accidentally instructed to increase its feed rate to 80 percent; a correction about twelve seconds later did not register, and the pump appears to have run at a much higher rate than commanded for about 3.25 hours, producing a fluoride overfeed. Together with a water main break the next day, this led to a water shortage. The text does not say how the overfeed was stopped, only that it was not resolved until after 2:40 p.m.
servicos_afetados: Drinking water supply in Orange County (Chapel Hill and Carrboro)

descricao.texto: A lead operator at the plant noticed the extra high fluoride levels.
trechos: A lead operator at the plant noticed the extra high levels "but did not take corrective action, leading to the issue not being resolved until after 2:40 p.m."

gatilho.texto: At 11:43 a.m. on February 2, a plant operator accidentally instructed the fluoride feed pump to increase its feed rate to 80 percent, compared with its normal operating range of about 8–12 percent.
trechos: According to the fluoride report, by CH2M HILL North Carolina, at 11:43 a.m. on February 2, a plant operator accidentally instructed the plant's fluoride feed pump to increase its feed rate to 80 percent, compared with its normal operating range of about 8–12 percent.

descricao.texto: An attempt to change the command about twelve seconds later did not register, according to the report; the pump appears to have operated at a rate significantly greater than the subsequent commanded speed for approximately 3.25 hours, resulting in a fluoride overfeed condition. No mechanism is given for why the change did not register.
trechos: The operator tried to change the command about twelve seconds later, but according to the report, the change didn't register.
"The pump appears to have operated at a rate significantly greater than the subsequent commanded speed for approximately 3.25 hours, resulting in a fluoride overfeed condition," the report says.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: The extra high levels were noticed at the plant but corrective action was not taken, and according to the report this led to the issue not being resolved until after 2:40 p.m.
trechos: A lead operator at the plant noticed the extra high levels "but did not take corrective action, leading to the issue not being resolved until after 2:40 p.m."

fatores_contribuintes.texto: A major water main break the next day, together with the extra fluoride dosage, prompted a water shortage; customers were unable to use or drink their water for more than twenty-four hours.
trechos: The extra fluoride dosage, plus a major water main break the next day, prompted a water shortage in Orange County that closed businesses, placed Chapel Hill and Carrboro under states of emergency, and sent residents scrambling to buy bottled water.
Customers were unable to use or drink their water for more than twenty-four hours.

acoes.texto: The OWASA board agreed that OWASA would develop solutions to prevent the particular failures, assess outage risks more broadly, take action to improve water system resiliency, and review communication practices during critical events.
trechos: “Last night, the Board agreed that OWASA would develop solutions to prevent the particular failures of last week, assess outage risks more broadly and take action to improve the water system resiliency, and review communication practices of OWASA and its partners during critical events.

acoes.texto: Already done: OWASA says it has stopped adding fluoride to the water; the agency is reportedly reviewing its policies and seeking public input before reintroducing it.
trechos: OWASA says it has stopped adding fluoride to the water, and
*The News & Observer*reports that the agency is reviewing its policies and seeking public input before reintroducing it to the water supply.
"The pump appears to have operated at a rate significantly greater than the subsequent commanded speed for approximately 3.25 hours, resulting in a fluoride overfeed condition," the report says.

motivo_confianca_baixa: causa_raiz.status: 'incerta' vs 'vaga' (the failed correction is stated but its mechanism is not, and the pump behavior is hedged with 'appears'); prevencao.nivel: 'genericas' vs 'especificas' (stopping fluoride addition is checkable but is a suspension rather than a named mechanism); duracao: 195 minutes (overfeed condition) vs null (customer impact was 'more than twenty-four hours' and combined with the water main break).
observacoes: The text gives no year for February 2. The document also covers a separate water main break on February 3; it is included only as a contributing factor because the text links it to the water shortage. The fluoride level recorded was 5.90 mg/L, exceeding state and federal primary drinking water standards by 1.9 mg/L.
